subject: Plan curation and seat-split options for CarePilot - negotiating discount tiers
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@carepilot.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Plan curation and seat-split options for CarePilot - negotiating discount tiers

Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation I attached a tightened proposal (carepilot_proposal_v2.pdf) with two curated pack options your engineering and procurement teams asked about:

- Option A (Throughput-first): higher seat pool, small set of premium features enabled (priority routing, KV cache expiry controls).
- Option B (Feature-first): smaller seat pool, full feature bundle (advanced tracing, extended retention).

Key asks for you:
- Confirm which option maps to your short-term priority (throughput vs. observability).
- Tell us target headcount usage for Q1 so we can sketch a seat-split and bursting plan.
- Procurement: Alicia, can you share the preferred discount threshold (e.g., commit $X/mo or Y% multi-year) so we can model concessions?

I included a simple seat-split workbook (seat-split-chart.xlsx) with a suggested 60/40 burst/steady split — Priya, see the assumptions tab for token distributions.

If it helps, happy to run a 30-minute workshop with your infra + procurement next week to walk the tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: carepilot_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF), seat-split-chart.xlsx (Spreadsheet)

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@carepilot.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@carepilot.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Plan curation and seat-split options for CarePilot - negotiating discount tiers

Ben —

Appreciate the clear options. A few quick notes from our side:

- Our immediate priority is throughput (latency sensitive features for live triage). Option A looks like the right direction.
- Q1 headcount: we expect ~35 active engineers calling the API with burst windows up to 150 concurrent inference requests.
- Procurement asked whether a 12-month committed spend would unlock a 15% discount, or if that requires a larger commit. Can you confirm the thresholds?

Also curious about the feature-gating: if we start on Option A and later add the observability bundle, is there a pro-rated path or do we need to switch plans?

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering, CarePilot
agomez@carepilot.com

--
Procurement: if you want a single doc with the final price ladder for our review, we'll share internally once we have Ben's thresholds.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@carepilot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Plan curation and seat-split options for CarePilot - negotiating discount tiers

Alicia —

Thanks — quick follow-up with thresholds and add-on behavior to make procurement's life easier:

Pricing thresholds (ballpark; can formalize once commit level is known):
- No commitment (pay-as-you-go): list rates, no discount.
- 12-month minimum commit >= $60k/month: eligible for 10% standard volume discount.
- 12-month minimum commit >= $120k/month: eligible for 15% discount + waived onboarding credit.
- 24-month multi-year >= $100k/month: eligible for 18% discount + extended SLA uplift.

Plan migration and add-ons:
- You can start on Option A and add the observability bundle later. Migration is additive — we prorate the bundle for the remainder of the billing period.
- If you switch core seat allocation (e.g., from throughput-first seats to feature-first seats) we treat that as a plan change; partial month proration applies.

Seat/burst guidance based on your numbers (35 active devs / 150 concurrent bursts):
- Suggest base pool of 60 seats for steady-state with a 3x burst buffer (configured as burst capacity) tied to autoscale triggers.
- Estimated token consumption (Q1) ~ 450M tokens/month at current usage pattern. See seat-split-chart assumptions.

I've attached a short SOC2 evidence overview you requested for procurement's security checklist (SOC2-evidence-overview.pdf).

If procurement wants a formal quote with two tiered commit options we can produce that by Friday.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-overview.pdf

From: Procurement Team <procure@carepilot.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@carepilot.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Plan curation and seat-split options for CarePilot - negotiating discount tiers

Ben/Priya —

Procurement here. A couple of clarifying points before we move to an internal approval:

1) We can greenlight a 12-month commit, but the execs prefer to see an option that keeps upside optional. Can you show:
   - A $65k/mo commit (baseline) with a 12% discount and a capped overage rate; and
   - A $125k/mo commit with 16% discount and a 6-month exit clause (with defined ramp-down terms).
2) We need clarity on how feature entitlements map to SLA (is observability tied to a different uptime measurement?).
3) Final ask: send a line-item quote (CSV or spreadsheet) with proration examples so our finance team can run scenarios.

If you can get a draft quote by Thursday we can route it through legal and finance the following week.

Thanks,
CarePilot Procurement
procure@carepilot.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Acquisition Decision <procure@carepilot.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@carepilot.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T16:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Plan curation and seat-split options for CarePilot - negotiating discount tiers

Procurement / Alicia —

Thanks for the clarity. We've put together a draft line-item quote (attached in the HubSpot record and the DocuSign link) that contains the two formal commit options you requested:

- Option 1: $65,000/mo commit (12-month) — 12% discount, capped overage at list rate + 25%, no early-exit credit.
- Option 2: $125,000/mo commit (12-month with 6-month exit) — 16% discount, capped overage at list rate + 15%, 50% credit for unused committed months within the ramp-down window (terms defined in clause 3.2).

Observability & SLA notes: observability bundle includes extended traces and 90-day metric retention. SLA uplift (99.9% -> 99.95%) is available for Option 2 as part of the multi-year uplift. We'll include explicit SLA measurements in the quote appendix.

Next steps:
- I've attached the CSV line items in the HubSpot record (see link above) and dropped a DocuSign envelope for Option 2 for faster turn. If you want Option 1 we can issue a separate envelope.
- Marissa will follow up with a short demo of the observability features once you sign the PO so you can validate the retention/trace behavior.

Marissa / Priya — please hold the onboarding credit for the Option 2 path until legal finalizes.

Alicia — let me know if you'd like the workshop before signature; otherwise we'll plan onboarding for the week after sign.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
